title: How To Avoid Angry Parent Complaints
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin addresses a common source of teacher anxiety: angry, confrontational parents. Drawing on stories submitted by readers, he argues that nearly all parent complaints stem from the same root cause — a teacher who has not clearly and publicly established how misbehavior will be handled. His proposed remedy is a three-step process built around transparency and documentation. First, teachers should send home a copy of their classroom management plan during the first week of school and get a signed acknowledgment from parents. Second, they should walk parents through the plan in detail at back-to-school night, framing it as protecting every child's right to learn. Third, and most importantly, teachers must consistently follow through on what they've promised, since having made a public commitment makes consistency easier to sustain. Linsin asserts that when this groundwork is laid, complaints become rare, and if one does surface, it is directed at the impartial plan rather than at the teacher personally.
points: Nearly all angry-parent complaints trace back to a teacher's use of an unclear or inconsistently applied disciplinary approach.
Sending home a signed acknowledgment of the classroom management plan creates an on-record understanding with parents.
Reviewing the plan in detail at back-to-school night pre-empts confusion and builds parent trust.
Publicly promising to follow the plan makes day-to-day consistency easier to maintain.
When complaints do arise, they become about the impartial plan rather than a personal grievance against the teacher.
quotes: Here at SCM, we’ve heard horror stories about angry parents .
In every case, it’s in response to how the teacher handled misbehavior.
The idea is to get parents on record of knowing full well the behavior expectations of the class and how students will be held accountable.
If you go back on your word, if you lecture, scold, or allow misbehavior to go without consequence, you open yourself up to complaints that are very difficult to defend against.
The secret to avoiding parent complaints is to lay bare the ins and outs of your classroom management plan from day one.
In 99.9 percent of cases, parents complain because their child’s right to learn is being trampled on. They complain because their child has to endure an environment of chaos.
